messages:
elle: Quick one  we have an employee on an approved LOA (medical) from 11/15 through 1/15. They were on payroll 12/31 but were on unpaid LOA that pay period. Can they carry over PTO into next year or do we treat them as ineligible?
ryan: Short answer: we usually require active payroll status (paid or unpaid leave can differ). Which LOA policy is this under? Medical vs parental changes things.
emily: Policy excerpt pasted below.
hr-bot: ```
Carryover eligibility: Employees who are active on payroll on 12/31 are eligible for carryover up to the published cap. Employees on unpaid LOA that causes them to be off-payroll on 12/31 are not eligible unless People Ops approves an exception. Medical LOA exceptions can be granted case-by-case.```
elle: In this case the employee is on unpaid medical LOA but still technically on the employee roster; payroll shows zero earnings that period. Manager asked if we can make an exception given the medical nature.
ryan: We can approve exceptions for medical LOA where using PTO during treatment or return is impractical. Need manager justification + HR approval + brief legal review.
emily: Suggested workflow: manager submits People Ops request with case notes, attach physician note if provided, and indicate desired carryover days (max up to cap). People Ops will route to payroll to tag the carryover if approved.
payroll-bot: FYI: If approved, payroll must receive the carryover tag by Jan 7 to apply in the new-year accrual run. Late tags require manual adjustment.
elle: Thanks  I'll ask the manager to submit the request. Can we draft a short template message for managers to use when requesting LOA-related carryover exceptions?
emily: Sure, draft below: "Manager request: Employee name, employee ID, LOA dates, LOA type (medical), justification for carryover exception, requested carryover days (<=cap), attachments (physician note or employee consent)."
elle: Perfect. I'll send that and close the loop. :pray:
